classification.difficultyReason: Part (a) requires parameterising opposite roots, coordinating all four coefficient relations, and choosing multiplication and squaring to eliminate parameters without dividing by possibly zero coefficients. Part (b) uses the familiar repeated-root parameterisation and eliminates its sum and product. The unsupplied elimination choices in part (a) set the whole-block demand.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The polynomial $P(x)=x^4+ax^3+bx^2+cx+d$ has two zeroes that are opposites. Show that $a^2d+c^2=abc$.

answer.short: Taking the zeroes as $t,-t,u,v$, the sum and triple-product relations give $c=-at^2$, and the pair and product relations give $d=-t^2(b+t^2)$. Eliminating $t^2$ gives $a^2d+c^2=abc$.
answer.worked:
Let the zeroes be $t,-t,u,v$.

Sum of roots:
$$u+v=-a\qquad(1)$$
Sum of products two at a time:
$$\begin{align*}-t^2+tu+tv-tu-tv+uv&=b\\uv-t^2&=b\qquad(2)\end{align*}$$
Sum of products three at a time:
$$\begin{align*}-t^2u-t^2v+tuv-tuv&=-c\\-t^2(u+v)&=-c\qquad(3)\end{align*}$$
Product of roots:
$$-t^2uv=d\qquad(4)$$
Substitute (1) into (3):
$$\begin{align*}-t^2(-a)&=-c\\c&=-at^2\qquad(5)\end{align*}$$
Substitute (2) into (4):
$$\begin{align*}d&=-t^2(b+t^2)\\a^2d&=-a^2bt^2-a^2t^4\qquad(6)\end{align*}$$
From (5), $c^2=a^2t^4$ and $abc=-a^2bt^2$. Add $c^2$ to (6):
$$\begin{align*}a^2d+c^2&=-a^2bt^2\\&=abc.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: The polynomial equation $x^4+px^3+qx^2+rx+s=0$ has two pairs of equal roots. Show that $p^3-4pq+8r=0$.

answer.short: Taking the roots as $t,t,u,u$, the sum and pair relations give $tu=\dfrac{4q-p^2}{8}$, and the triple relation gives $r=p\,tu$. Eliminating $tu$ gives $p^3-4pq+8r=0$.
answer.worked:
Let the roots be $t,t,u,u$.

Sum of roots:
$$\begin{align*}2t+2u&=-p\\t+u&=-\frac p2\qquad(1)\end{align*}$$
Sum of products two at a time:
$$\begin{align*}t^2+4tu+u^2&=q\\(t+u)^2+2tu&=q\qquad(2)\end{align*}$$
Sum of products three at a time:
$$\begin{align*}2t^2u+2tu^2&=-r\\2tu(t+u)&=-r\qquad(3)\end{align*}$$
Substitute (1) into (2):
$$\begin{align*}\frac{p^2}{4}+2tu&=q\\tu&=\frac{4q-p^2}{8}\qquad(4)\end{align*}$$
Substitute (1) into (3):
$$\begin{align*}2tu\left(-\frac p2\right)&=-r\\r&=p\,tu\qquad(5)\end{align*}$$
Substitute (4) into (5):
$$\begin{align*}r&=\frac{p(4q-p^2)}{8}\\8r&=4pq-p^3\\p^3-4pq+8r&=0.\end{align*}$$
